Donald Margulies' new Broadway play, "Time Stands Still," fixates on an old journalism-school question: Can recording human suffering to tell the world morally suffice for doing nothing in the moment to stop it?

Donald Margulies' new play 'Time Stands Still' is a thoughtful drama about a war photographer and her journalist boyfriend dealing with trauma and relationships, but it feels more like a well-crafted TV movie than essential theater.
Donald Margulies has written a play about four people who talk about their problems for two hours, and while they're all articulate and their problems are real, the talk never quite adds up to drama.
Margulies has never written characters quite as tortured as these in the intensely moving Time Stands Still.

In its limited run, Time Stands Still was one of last season's best new plays and among the most satisfying evenings on Broadway. Its return open run, with Ricci's replacement of Alicia Silverstone the only cast change and the three returning actors giving even richer performances, is bound to be among this season's cream as well.
Christina Ricci makes an admirable Broadway debut as the perky character originated by Alicia Silverstone but otherwise the show has changed little in the process.
